topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The opening framing welcomes students, introduces the lecture on cancer evolution, and outlines the session's learning outcomes.

topics.label: Clonal selection and epigenetic drivers of tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how sequential genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer competitive growth advantages that drive Darwinian clonal succession.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the role of tissue hierarchies, cancer stem cells, and cell-of-origin identity in tumor initiation and propagation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental influences and stromal support in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how environmental promoters, chronic inflammation, and supportive stroma create permissive conditions for tumor outgrowth and maintenance.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the genomic, spatial omics, and computational technologies used to investigate evolutionary trajectories and cellular interactions in tumors.

topics.label: Integrated multifactorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the interplay among mutational burden, cell-of-origin properties, and microenvironmental triggers in shaping cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The closing framing wraps up the lecture and provides a preview of the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
